title: Attention as In-Context Empirical Bayes: A Two-Stage View via Particle Dynamics
claim: A two-stage procedure first refines a sample-based prior through depth, then infers a posterior from the original noisy query, matching reverse diffusion in the limit.
layout: 3 panels: wide top pipeline left-to-right, two insets below; dashed skip arrow
description: Panel (a) across the top is a left-to-right pipeline. Orange noisy tokens scattered around a ring enter a gray Stage 1 self-attention box (particle refinement over L layers). A ring of blue particles, the learned particle prior, comes out and goes into a purple Stage 2 cross-attention box (posterior mean E[x_i | x̃_i, ρ̂_0]). The output is a pale blue ring, the clean estimate. A dashed curved arrow runs under the whole pipeline and carries the noisy query directly to Stage 2. Below it are two rounded insets. Panel (b) shows orange scattered points becoming blue points and then a tight cluster at layer ℓ=0, ℓ*/2 and ℓ*, with arrows between them. Panel (c) shows a blurry orange ring becoming a sharp blue ring through idealized reverse diffusion, with equations under it. Orange means noisy and blue means clean, which guides the eye.
caption: (a) Collective in-context denoising: Multilayer attention implements a two-stage EB procedure. Depth iteratively refines a particle prior (Stage 1), while a long-range skip--- acting as an Attention Residual (AttnRes)---enables posterior averaging with the initial noisy input as query (Stage 2). (b) Particle dynamics: Discrete self-attention updates move corrupted tokens from their initial noised distribution toward high-density regions of the underlying clean prior. (c) Theoretical limit: In the large-context, continuous-depth regime, these dynamics recover an anti-diffusive denoising operator consistent with a reverse diffusion process.
abstract: We study minimal attention-only transformers under all-token corruption and show they admit a two-stage empirical Bayes interpretation. A single attention step computes a kernel-weighted posterior mean with respect to the empirical distribution defined by the context. Depth refines this distribution through particle dynamics (Stage 1), while a long-range skip-connection carries the noisy input as a query for posterior inference (Stage 2), revealing distinct statistical roles for depth and attention residuals. The framework isolates a minimal setting in which the context itself induces a depth-dependent energy landscape governing in-context inference. We show that effective denoising can emerge without an explicit noise schedule: a fixed kernel bandwidth and finite integration horizon suffice, yielding a principled depth-noise relationship. We further establish a posterior-mean recovery guarantee for Gaussian priors, showing the empirical estimator converges to the Bayes-optimal predictor under sequential asymptotic conditions. Connecting these dynamics to reverse-diffusion limits, our results provide a statistical interpretation of attention as in-context inference via sample-based posterior estimation, without explicit density modeling.
